Hi Dana —

Thanks for the clear list. I've attached an updated dataflow diagram and our current subprocessor roster for your review (see files: redwood_dataflow_v2.pdf, subprocessor_roster_20261125.csv). High level answers below; Kim and Priyom are looped for technical and legal follow-up.

- Telemetry scope: our runtime emits two classes of telemetry:
  1) Operational telemetry (metrics, scheduler traces, GPU utilization) — never includes user prompt content.
  2) Inference traces (latency buckets, token counts, error codes, and optionally sampled anonymized prompt hashes) — sampling and hashing/prefix-preservation applied; raw prompt text is not included in observability exports by default.
- Subprocessors: roster includes cloud infra (compute), metrics/observability provider, and analytics partner. The CSV includes processing country and statement of purpose for each.
- Cross-border: production inference occurs in customer-configured regions. Backups and analytics jobs may run in our analytics region (us-west-2) or EU region for customers that opted into EU residency; the roster flags these.

Open questions for you: do you need a certified statement (evidence pack) for KMS custody and key separation, or will the edited dataflow + roster be sufficient for the DPO screening?

We can set up a short call Friday or early next week to walk through the artifacts.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Brightwell SSQ: telemetry slicing, subprocessor delegation, and transfer paths

Hi Dana —

Thanks for the questions. I'll take the technical lead on these answers:

1) Prompt hashing: hashes are HMAC-SHA256 with a per-customer salt stored in a KMS-backed secrets store. The salt is managed per-customer and can be rotated; without the salt the hashes are not reversible. Original prompt text is not retained in the observability pipeline. The only place full request text may exist is ephemeral worker memory during live inference and in customer-configured request logs if the customer explicitly enables "retain raw prompts for X days" in their project settings (this is opt-in and off by default).

2) Analytics partner flow: Redwood transforms the stream before any external transfer. The transformation pipeline (applied in-region within the customer's residency when required) includes:
  - Prompt hashing (customer-salt HMAC) for sampled prompts
  - PII redaction rules (pre-configured regex + entity recognition) that replace detected fields with deterministic tokens (e.g., <EMAIL_1>, <SSN_1>)
  - Truncation of prompt tails beyond a configured token budget for traces
All transforms occur in our transform service (hosted by Redwood) prior to export; subprocessors never receive unredacted raw prompts unless the customer has explicitly enabled raw-log export and granted consent.

3) Retention:
  - Sampled traces (hashed/pseudonymized): 90 days by default, configurable down to 7 days on request.
  - Operational metrics (non-content): 540 days for system analytics and capacity planning.
  - Debug logs containing raw prompts: 7 days by default and require a customer opt-in; with opt-in retention never exceeds 90 days unless the customer requests longer retention in writing.

4) Backups / DR exports: regular backups of configuration and non-content metrics may be replicated to our DR region (us-east-1) and, for customers with EU residency enabled, to eu-central-1. Backups do not include raw prompt content or unredacted PII; if a customer has enabled raw-log export as described above, backups will contain that data and we annotate it in the roster.

I've attached a KMS custody matrix that maps which keys are customer-managed vs Redwood-managed (kms_custody_matrix.xlsx) and a short extract of the subprocessor roster showing processing regions.

If it helps, we can provide a one‑page signed exhibit confirming these retention windows and transform behaviours for procurement/DPA purposes. Also happy to walk through the transform pipeline with your engineering team.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Architecture
Redwood Inference

Attachments: kms_custody_matrix.xlsx
